transcript.content: Hi, welcome. What brings you in today?

Well, I came in today because... for a while now, I’ve been dealing with something that's been hard to shake. I work as a personal financial advisor, and I've been convinced lately that certain people in the arts and finance circles here in Cincinnati are quietly tracking which clients I meet with. 

And it feels like they're sending me little signals about it. I'll notice it in the invitations I get, or the panel topics at networking events, or even just who ends up sitting near me. I mean, I try to tell myself it could just be a coincidence, but... I can’t really let it go. It just stays with me, so I thought I should probably talk to someone about it.
About how long have you been feeling convinced that these people are tracking your clients?
I'd say it's been going on for about two months now. Yeah, it was around two months ago that I really started noticing the signals and feeling like they were tracking my meetings.
During this time, have you been needing much less sleep than usual without feeling tired?

No, I wouldn't say that. I've been sleeping about the same amount as I usually do, maybe seven or eight hours a night. I haven't noticed any changes there, and I definitely still feel tired if I don't get enough rest.
Have you been hearing voices when no one else is around?
No, I haven't experienced anything like that. I don't hear voices or anything when I'm alone. It's really just the signals and the feeling that I'm being tracked.
Have you been feeling depressed most of the day nearly every day?

No, not really. I mean... I get stressed out about the tracking, obviously, but I wouldn't say I'm depressed. My mood has been pretty normal, honestly. I don't feel down all day or anything like that.
Aside from feeling that these people are tracking your clients and sending signals, have you had any other unusual beliefs that others say aren’t true?

No, I don't think so. It's really just the tracking and the signals I mentioned. I haven't had any other... unusual ideas, or things that people have told me aren't true. It's pretty much just confined to the situation with my clients.
Have you found yourself talking much less than usual lately?

Yeah, I guess I have been. When friends ask what's going on with me, I mostly just give them really short answers. It just... I don't know, talking feels like more effort than it should lately. 

And I guess that kind of goes for other things, too. I still get my work done in pieces, but I just don't have the same spark. Like, I'll just leave client follow-ups sitting there. I've also been skipping my usual jazz nights and pickup basketball games, and... I don't really feel much about missing them, to be honest.
At any point since this started, did the belief that people were tracking your clients go away completely for at least a few days?
No, it hasn't gone away. Since I first noticed it, it's been pretty constant. There hasn't been a time where I thought, "Oh, they stopped tracking them." It's just... always there.
Have you felt that your emotions seem flatter than usual, like your face or voice shows less feeling?

I haven't really noticed that, to be honest. I mean, nobody has pointed out that I look or sound any different. I think my expressions and the way I talk are just... normal for me. I don't feel like I'm flatter or showing less emotion, just maybe a bit more tired or quiet.
Have other people told you that your speech has been hard to follow or that you jump from one idea to another?

No, no one has said anything like that to me. I know I've been giving shorter answers lately, but when I do talk, people seem to understand me just fine. I don't think I jump around from topic to topic, and... well, none of my friends or clients have complained that I'm hard to follow. So, no.
Since this started, has it been going on for more than one month?
Yeah, it's been longer than a month. I'd say the whole thing—feeling like people are tracking my client meetings and sending me signals—has been going on for about two months now.
Do you believe these people can somehow know about your client meetings without any normal way of finding out?

No, I don't think it's anything impossible like mind reading, if that's what you mean. I figure they just... hack into my phone or my work calendar. Or maybe they have someone watching my office. There are plenty of regular, technical ways they could be getting the information about my schedule without it being anything supernatural.
Since this started, has your work or day-to-day functioning dropped noticeably compared with how you were before?

Yeah, I'd say it has. I mean, I'm still working, but my practice has definitely gotten smaller lately. I just... I end up missing follow-ups, and I've been avoiding some of the public panels I usually speak at. It's just been a lot harder to keep up the same level of day-to-day client contact that I used to manage before all this started.
Have you been finding it much harder to get yourself started on things, even routine tasks?

Yeah, it really has been. I mean, I still manage to get my work done, but just in pieces. I just don't have the same spark I used to. Like, I'll just leave client follow-ups sitting there. And it's not just work... I've been skipping out on jazz nights and my usual pickup basketball games, and honestly, I don't even feel much about missing them. When my friends ask what's going on with me, I just give them really short answers. It just... talking just feels like way more effort than it should right now.
Do you avoid panels and follow-ups mainly because you feel watched there?

No, not really. I mean, the whole thing with feeling like they're tracking my schedule is stressful, sure, but... that's not why I'm skipping things. It's more just... I don't have the energy for it. Like I said, I just don't have the drive to do those things anymore. It's not about avoiding them because I'm scared or feeling watched, it's just... I just don't care enough to put the effort in right now.
